title: Control-channel SSL renegotiate causing firewall idle teardown - incident journal
body:
Summary:

Short: During a scheduled incremental TLS certificate rotation on the private control channel (primary -> standby handoff), a subset of customer-managed stateful firewalls aggressively timed out TCP flows during brief SSL renegotiation bursts. That led to repeated control-channel disconnects for ~35 minutes for 14 customers in region eu-west-2. Service impact: control-plane RPC failures and delayed config push; dataplane inference continued but some control-plane initiated operations (policy updates, live rollouts) stalled.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture timeline and quick mitigations used during the oncall shift.
- Draft a minimal runbook checklist for future TLS rotations when behind stateful customer firewalls.
- Record hypotheses & follow-ups for infra and solutions teams.

High-level impact:
- Affected tenants: 14 private/VPC deployments (eu-west-2).
- Symptoms: repeated TLS session drops between node-agent <-> controlplane, grpc reset errors, intermittent p99 control API latency spikes, rollout failures.
- User-visible: delayed canary rollouts, delayed config-sync, some management-plane API errors surfaced to tenant dashboards. No inference data-plane data loss observed.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-09-02 02:12 UTC: Rotation job kickoff (staggered per cluster) — automated pipeline applied new certs to controlplane-primary.
- 02:18 UTC: Pager triggered by p95 control-plane grpc error rate crossing threshold for eu-west-2 cluster A. Oncall (Asha) alerted.
- 02:21 UTC: Observed burst patterns: short-lived SSL renegotiations (10–30s) across multiple control-channel TCP connections.
- 02:25 UTC: Customers with edge firewalls that enforce aggressive idle TCP/NAT timeouts (sub-60s) started showing persistent reconnects.
- 02:30 UTC: Rolled rollback on cert rotation for cluster A (stop further rotation) — partial mitigation; errors shifted to cluster B where rotation was still progressing.
- 02:33–02:47 UTC: We applied temporary keepalive increase on control channel endpoints for clusters in the affected region via emergency flag (tcp_keepalive & grpc keepalive interval increase).
- 02:48 UTC: Error volume decreased but not resolved for some customers that have mid-path firewalls doing deep packet inspection (DPI) and re-evaluating TLS sessions during renegotiation.
- 02:55 UTC: Customer success engaged for tenants with managed firewalls; suggested opening firewall logs and raising idle timeout to >120s.
- 03:24 UTC: Rotation paused globally until we have a longer-term plan.
- 03:30 UTC: Incident declared resolved for majority of tenants; followup tasks created for further hardening.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Stop/rollback ongoing certificate rotations in-progress in eu-west-2.
- Ramp-up grpc keepalive ping frequency and tcp_keepalive probes to prevent firewall idle timeouts during the transition window. Commands used (examples):
  - sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=30
  - export GRPC_KEEPALIVE_TIME_MS=20000 (service env injection during emergency flag)
- Applied an emergency routing rule to prefer in-region redundant control-channel endpoints that did not yet rotate to new certs for affected tenants.
- Notified Customer Success + Solutions (SL) to reach out to affected customers with instructions for firewall config adjustments.

Root cause hypothesis (short):
- The automated rotation triggered short-lived TLS session renegotiations and connection restarts. Several customer-managed network firewalls and DPI middleboxes are configured to aggressively clear state on unusual TLS session events (session renegotiation/resumption), treating renegotiation as a new connection or suspicious event. Their idle/NAT tracking then timed out or reset the session while controlplane and node-agent attempted to re-establish secure connections.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Packet captures from an affected tenant show ClientHello->Alert handshake sequences followed by TCP RSTs originating at the customer firewall.
- Firewall logs from two customers indicate session state cleared with reason code referencing SSL session change.
- Regions where rotation was delayed or not yet applied did not show errors.

Non-root causes we ruled out quickly:
- Controlplane cert chain validity: certs valid and chain verified for endpoints that stayed up.
- Net flaps due to BGP: no routing changes in cloud provider logs correlated to the time window.
- Memory/conntrack exhaustion: host metrics within normal ranges.

Draft short-runbook (operational checklist) - to include in oncall playbook:
1) Pre-rotation checklist for private/VPC tenants:
   - Identify tenants behind managed/third-party firewalls with aggressive DPI/NAT idle policies. Tag them in our rotation plan and contact them before rotation.
   - Schedule rotation with a maintenance window and optional keepalive override.
2) Preflight tests (staged):
   - Canary: rotate a single controlplane node and observe for >= 30 min.
   - Verify keepalive and tcp probe settings are in place (GRPC and system-level).
3) During rotation (if any sign of increased TLS renegotiation):
   - Pause further rotation in region and roll back the change where safe.
   - Immediately set GRPC_KEEPALIVE and tcp_keepalive to conservative values (e.g., probe <= 20s) for control-channel services.
   - Flag affected tenants and switch traffic to non-rotated control endpoints if available.
4) If RSTs persist and firewall contact is possible:
   - Ask customer to allowlist controlplane endpoint IPs and to increase TCP idle/NAT timeout to >= 120s during rotation.
   - Provide packet-capture snippet showing rationale.
5) Post-rotation:
   - Monitor for 3x normal rotation window, watch for grpc error rates, and confirm all control RPCs are healthy.

Quick commands & queries used during triage:
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=controlplane -o wide
- tcpdump -i ens160 host <customer-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/cc-rotate.pcap
- gcloud logging read "resource.labels.region="europe-west2" AND severity>=ERROR" --limit 200
- curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://controlplane-eu-west2.redwood.internal:443/status
- grpcurl -insecure -proto control.proto controlplane:443 Service.HealthCheck

Followups / Action items (owners & ETA):
- Solutions eng (Jonas) -> Build standard pre-rotation notification template for tenants behind stateful firewalls. ETA: 2026-09-09.
- Infra (Priya) -> Add a rotation gating flag that enforces keepalive overrides automatically during rotations; add region-level pause on high grpc error velocity. ETA: 2026-09-16.
- SRE (Asha) -> Update oncall runbook with the checklist above and include sample sysctl/GRPC env vars. ETA: 2026-09-06.
- Security/Compliance (Marco) -> Validate that keepalive changes are acceptable for compliance-sensitive customers; produce an advisory for customers with strict network controls. ETA: 2026-09-10.
- Engineering (team-wide) -> Evaluate whether we can shift to session-resumption-friendly rotation approach (use TLS 1.3 post-handshake auth flows / zero-downtime re-key path) to avoid renegotiation spikes. Ticket created: JIRA-INF-2201.

Notes & loose thoughts (for postmortem):
- Many vendor firewall appliances have heuristics that treat TLS behavior change as malware-like; our rotation pattern (short stagger + ephemeral renegotiations) is benign but trips those heuristics. We should maintain a small staging lane that mimics rotations behind those middleboxes to catch the behavior.
- Consider adding an explicit TCP-level keepalive handshake from the node-agent that signals "control-channel active" during rotation windows to reduce mid-path devices' tendency to clear state.
- For long-lived private connections, longer default keepalive intervals (policy) may reduce this class of incidents but could have latency/cost implications; weigh with product.

Appendix: Example firewall log snippet (anonymized):
[2026-09-02T02:19:46Z] SRC=10.5.32.8 DST=54.12.34.56 PROTO=TCP SPT=443 DPT=51873 ACTION=RESET REASON=TLS_SESSION_CHANGE

Appendix: Packet capture excerpt notes:
- Observed TLS 1.3 ServerHello then short Alert Received (protocol_version=TLSv1.3, description=unexpected_message) followed by TCP RST from firewall IP.

Draft slack blurb for affected tenants:
"Hi <customer>, we observed transient control-plane reconnects during our certificate rotation in eu-west-2 between 02:15-03:30 UTC. We've paused further rotations and applied temporary keepalive changes. To avoid further disruption we recommend setting your firewall/NAT idle timeout to >=120s for maintenance windows or allowlisting our control-plane IPs. Our Solutions team will reach out with tailored instructions. Apologies for the disruption — Asha (SRE)."

End of journal.
